ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, consolidated by the Law of 27 October 2020 and the Law of 25 January 2021 (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law, Memorial A No. 15 of 5 February 2019) with Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 (SCSp regime, Articles 944-1 to 944-11-1); Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions and business establishment permits; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement (acte de société), in private or notarial form, containing UBO schedules
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or the constituting partners; if executed abroad, apostilled by the competent foreign authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Luxembourg party since 3 June 1979); consular legalization required only for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and registry extract of any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry of the corporate general partner's state of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Convention states, consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners and the day-to-day manager (associé gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarized certified true copy admissible under the AML/CFT Law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility invoice or bank statement, issued within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certified true copy verified by the deposed professional

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation formalities, executed by all partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of execution or Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign signatures; consular legalization where the apostille regime does not apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (bulletin no. 3) of the proposed day-to-day manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Casier judiciaire du Luxembourg or equivalent foreign criminal-records authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; authenticity must be dated within 3 months of submission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, the managing partner and any corporate general-partner representatives against (i) the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law, (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Council Regulations 2580/2001 and 881/2002, (iii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, (iv) the OFAC SDN list for USD-clearing contingencies, and (v) national AEDT and CSSF designations. PEP status must be self-disclosed; any PEP exposure triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth substantiation and written approval by the AML compliance officer. Re-screening is obligatory upon any material ownership or management change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) electronic filing portal, www.lbr.lu and MyGuichet.lu one-stop-shop
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are accepted in French, German or Luxembourgish; French is the de facto documentary standard. The corporate name must use Latin-alphabet characters; a foreign-language or ideographic brand (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Latin script and the transliteration must be expressly recorded in the SCSp partnership agreement. The name must be distinctive, lawful, truthful and not misleading as to the legal form, activity or territorial origin of the undertaking.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Caisse d'épargne, Crédit (require CSSF banking authorization)
Assurance, Réassurance, Insurance (require insurance-sector ministerial authorization)
SICAV, FCP, OPCM, Fonds d'investissement, Fonds (require CSSF fund authorization)
Luxembourg, Lëtzebuerg, Grand-Duché, État (require prior approval of the Ministry of Justice)
Université, Académie, Lycée, École (require Ministry of Education assent)
Croix-Rouge, UNESCO, UNO and other protected international emblems
Words contrary to public policy, morality, or deceptive as to the nature of the trade or the SCSp legal form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR registrar issues a written non-availability decision upon request. Within 10 business days, the applicant may (1) submit an alternative name to maintain filing priority, (2) file a reasoned reconsideration request with the LBR registration division, and (3) if the registrar confirms rejection, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within one month of notification. The appeal is summary in nature and a decision is ordinarily rendered within 30 to 60 days. Where the rejection is based on a third-party trademark conflict, the applicant may simultaneously initiate cancellation or opposition proceedings before the Luxembourg Intellectual Property Office or EUIPO and refile the name after a favorable ruling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and domiciliation are permissible solely through a Luxembourg-licensed domiciliation agent for the registered seat. The SCSp must nevertheless maintain genuine commercial substance in Luxembourg: a physically leased tea-salon and ceramics showroom, locally maintained books and records, a Luxembourg bank account, and local social-security and payroll arrangements for any staff. A pure mailbox or letterbox model is incompatible with the food-and-beverage establishment permit and the AML/CFT substance expectations of the RBE regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced food-safety hygiene inspections by the Luxembourg food-safety administration (ASV) carry a probability exceeding 80 percent within the first 24 months of operation. Unannounced substance and anti-abuse audits by the Luxembourg direct-tax administration (AEDT) for this low-risk retail pass-through entity are estimated at under 10 percent in the first year. Merchant-acquiring banks reserve a contractual right to perform on-site merchant review at least once every 12 to 36 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, including the provisions on the société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on accounting and annual accounts of undertakings, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic filings are submitted through the MyGuichet.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS application for registration of an SCSp, accompanied by the deed of constitution (acte constitutif/contrat de société), submitted via the RCS electronic filing system; subsequent mandatory publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum subscribed or paid-up capital and no requirement to deposit funds in an escrow account. Contributions may be in cash, in kind, or in services, and are governed solely by the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the limited partnership agreement is approved and constituted as the SCSp charter. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and recorded in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [general partner] is appointed gérant of the SCSp, authorised, jointly or severally, to complete all statutory filings, to instruct publication in the Electronic Register of Companies and Associations, and to open a professional bank account. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial capital contribution schedule contained in the partnership agreement is ratified, such contributions to be credited with immediate effect, and the authorised gérant is instructed to carry out all required formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request to the LBR, including the legal form suffix 'SCSp'. The LBR will verify that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to existing business names, civil companies, protected designations, or trademarks. The name reservation is valid for two months and may be renewed upon expiry.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in up to three alternatives with the 'SCSp' suffix
Passport copy of the requesting general partner
Correspondence address of the future registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for identity or misleading similarity, submit a new application with a more distinctive descriptor; no formal appeal is available, but a revised name can be filed immediately without loss of priority if resubmitted within the initial one-week period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The general partner(s), assisted by counsel; a Luxembourg notary if notarisation is elected
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in French or English, setting out the legal form (SCSp), registered office, corporate object, duration, capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing, gérant appointment, and voting rights. The deed may be executed under private signature or by notarial deed; notarisation is voluntary unless the SCSp holds Luxembourg real estate or enters into regulated transactions requiring authentication. All partners and the gérant must execute the deed before RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Full identity particulars and passport copies of each partner
Draft limited partnership agreement (acte de société)
Valuation statement for any non-cash contribution
Written acceptance of appointment by the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS clerk rejects a private deed for incomplete statutory content, execute a supplementary deed correcting the omitted clauses; the filing is treated as valid once the complement is lodged within the registrar’s cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu / LBR e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RCS creation request electronically by selecting the SCSp legal form, completing the register control data, uploading the signed partnership agreement and name reservation, and paying the filing fee. The registrar verifies the legal conformity of the deed, the identity and authorisation of the gérant, and the availability of the name. Registration is constitutive of the SCSp’s existence vis-à-vis third parties and permits the opening of a professional bank account.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (acte de société)
Name reservation confirmation issued by the LBR
Criminal record extract (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the gérant
Certificate of no minimum paid-up capital, if applicable
Declaration of acceptance by the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or request for rectification, respond within fifteen calendar days by uploading a correcting statement or a supplementary deed; if the application is rejected, refile within seven days without losing chronological priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Register of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration entry to the RESA for publication. Verify that the published notice contains the legal form, RCS number, registered office, object, and gérant identification. The publication evidences the SCSp’s legal existence and is required before the certificate of registration can be used for banking or licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the deed of constitution
RCS filing and publication receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, file a written rectification request with the RCS and, if necessary, seek an order from the President of the District Court to ensure third-party reliance is not harmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Administrative Setup: VAT, Social Security, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); selected Luxembourg commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply to the AEDT for the VAT identification number, register the gérant and employees with the CCSS, and open a professional bank account in the name of the SCSp. The bank will require the RCS extract, the deed of constitution, and the identity documents of authorised signatories. Municipal notification of the commercial address must also be made for the future establishment licence.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation extract
VAT registration form (formulaire 102)
Original or notarised copy of the partnership agreement
Passport copies of the gérant and all authorised signatories
Bank mandate signatures for the SCSp account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays the VAT number, submit a formal reminder and request an interim identification number. If a bank refuses the account mandate, provide a clean RCS extract and updated identity documents to another Luxembourg bank; any shortcoming in the social security registration may be cured by late declaration plus payment of penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate of Business Establishment and Commerce; municipal authorities for siting and public opening of the tea salon lounge
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d’établissement (business establishment licence) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to regulated professions and the holding of commercial establishments; if prepared food and beverages are served, a food business registration or approval from the Ministry of Health is also required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) operated under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D – low-impact service establishment; environmental registration only, no full EIA report required for a tea salon with seating below 200 persons and without industrial-scale preparation or extractive ventilation; municipal sewage and waste handling conditions apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge of wastewater must comply with the municipal drainage regulation (pH 6.0–10.0, BOD5 below 400 mg/L, COD below 1000 mg/L, TSS below 600 mg/L). A grease trap is mandatory if any food preparation involves oils exceeding 10 g per serving. Emissions of VOCs and odours from tea brewing are negligible; waste shall be withheld from the general municipal stream and collected by an authorised private waste operator under the Law of 5 March 2004 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire brigade and the Corps Grand-Ducal Incendie et de Secours; building occupancy permit from the commune validating public capacity, exit routes, fire retardancy, and structural load for seating and equipment; occupational health and safety inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for all staff areas; public liability insurance is a precondition for the issuance of the establishment licence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg VAT, excise and registration duties. Official portals: guichet.lu and myguichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SCSp without legal personality, the foreign partnership must first obtain a Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) national identification number (matricule) by filing the incorporation/registration dossier through a certified notary or authorized agent on myguichet.lu. After RCS enrolment, the entity must apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT registration (LU + 8-digit numeric ID) using the standard electronic registration form when making taxable supplies in Luxembourg or when engaged in intra-Community acquisitions subject to VAT. If the SCSp has no domestic permanent establishment, a Luxembourg VAT representative may be required; foreign partners must also provide their relevant foreign TIN and proof of legal existence. No minimum capital is required, but proof of a registered office in Luxembourg and identity of the general partner is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is fiscally transparent by default; the partnership agreement governs profit and loss allocation. Partners may elect to waive the Luxembourg small-enterprise VAT exemption (annual turnover threshold €30,000) and submit regular VAT returns. SCSp may opt into a Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) under the VAT Law. For income tax, no check-the-box mechanism exists; transparency is statutory. Hybrid mismatch elections may be available under ATAD/DAC6 and the Luxembourg tax anti-abuse rules, subject to EU law and preventing double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €30,000 (annual taxable turnover excluding VAT, for the small-enterprise exemption; registration is compulsory above this threshold or when making intra-EU acquisitions, importing goods, or without EU establishment supplying taxable services liable to Luxembourg VAT, in which case reverse-charge and/or registration obligations may apply)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or mandatory domestic B2B clearance exists in Luxembourg as of the current framework. B2G e-invoicing must be issued via the Peppol network under Luxembourg public procurement rules. All VAT invoices, including those for the tea salon lounge, must maintain authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility; XML/EDI electronic formats are accepted and an audit trail must be kept for at least 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT under Article 41 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided the goods leave EU territory and are accompanied by customs export declarations (EXA/EX1) and transport evidence. Intra-EU zero-rating (exempt with deductibility) applies to supplies to registered VAT customers in another Member State where VIES and EC Sales List requirements are met. Offshore services connected with export transport, handling, and services ancillary to export or import are zero-rated when performed for a customer established outside the EU; the salon's café/cultural service supplies to international visitors remain standard-rated unless dispatched as goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EXA or EX1, with MRN), Bill of Lading or AIR WAYBILL/CMR, Commercial Invoice (with HS codes and country of origin), Single Administrative Document, Proof of transport/freight movement, Delivery and receipt confirmation, Inward remittance / payment evidence, VIES VAT number validation evidence for intra-EU zero rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retroactively claw back zero-rated VAT where proof of export is deficient, inaccurate, falsified or not produced within statutory scrutiny periods. Default interest runs from the date VAT became chargeable (currently 0.8% per month or partial month). Administrative fines apply for VAT understatement or intentional evasion, and criminal penalties may be imposed for fraudulent export documentation, including fines up to €50,000 and imprisonment. The taxpayer must maintain all customs bills, transport evidence, payment receipts and counterparty VAT status evidence for at least 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct and AML oversight; European Central Bank (ECB) for eurozone monetary policy
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member with full capital and current account convertibility under EU treaty law and the ECB regulatory framework. There are no statutory exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittance, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. Dividend distributions require standard corporate formalities, audited financial statements where applicable, and tax withholding compliance under the Luxembourg domestic anti-abuse rules, but no administrative authorisation or conversion license is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Luxembourg. Export receipts, including those in foreign currency from specialty tea and ceramic exports, may be retained, converted, or hedged freely. There is no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline imposed by the BCL.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with structural caveats. A Luxembourg-licensed payment institution (PI) or EEA-authorized electronic money institution (EMI) may technically open payment accounts for an SCSp, but many offshore digital EMIs decline partnership structures due to complex KYC, transparency, and regulatory perimeter concerns. Viability is improved when the EMI holds a valid EEA passport, executes full FATCA/CRS reporting, and accepts the SCSp as a non-resident-tax-transparent vehicle under Luxembourg binding tax clearance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for SCSp corporate account opening in Luxembourg. Most tier-1 banks permit remote videoconference identification for directors, general partners, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) when the entity is EU-incorporated, documentation is correctly legalized/apostilled, and the approval chain is fully electronic. However, certain banks may require an in-person interview or visit for the authorised signatory if the UBO is resident in a high-risk third country or when the general partner is itself a non-EU corporate vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is not registered at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), creating no public corporate record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarised limited partnership agreement (LPA), a legal opinion confirming the non-registration is lawful for SCSp, identification of the general partner and its legal representatives, and notarised power-of-attorney appointing the account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partners benefit from statutory anonymity, making percentage of ownership and control difficult to verify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a certified internal register of all limited partners, a CSSF-compliant beneficial ownership declaration (RBE form), an organisational chart showing 25% or greater ownership interests, and a Luxembourg legal opinion interpreting limited partner rights as purely economic and non-controlling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from non-EEA or high-risk jurisdictions is classified as possible wealth concealment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide six months of bank statements of the contributing investor, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, warranty deeds, audited financial statements of the investor if applicable, and a certified transaction trail from the originating account to the Luxembourg escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax classification ambiguity of a pass-through SCSp triggers an incorrect FATCA/CRS self-certification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit an advance tax clearance ruling or a letter from the Luxembourg direct tax administration confirming the SCSp is tax transparent, along with completed Form W-9/W-8BEN-E where required and a CRS self-certification identifying the general partner as the reporting entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from investors must be wired via SWIFT MT103 using a clear reference to the SCSp name and the LP agreement. For ECB balance-of-payments reporting, use the purpose code 'D.1' or 'FDI' for direct investment contributions; for portfolio or equity-type injections use 'FOR' with a supplementary narrative. The receiving bank should be provided with the investor's identity, UBO percentage, source of funds evidence, and the notarised LPA prior to first deposit. If the investor is an EU entity, SEPA Credit Transfer can be used, preserving full traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for imported specialty loose-leaf tea, ceramic tableware, and lounge supplies should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for operational and low-value disbursements and SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary letters of credit for commercial bulk purchases. For EUR-denominated payments to EEA suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) are the highest-efficiency rail. For non-EUR disbursements, the bank's correspondent network will apply standard nostro clearing; transactions must reference the underlying commercial invoice, Incoterms, and the SCSp operational account to avoid anti-money-laundering delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/JPY)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency swaps qualifying for portfolio hedge accounting
Vanilla European-style FX options used for premium-limited risk coverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (depot des comptes annuels) - mandatory unless all general partners are natural persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than seven months after the financial year-end; calendar-year entity: 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial fine up to EUR 25,000; formal demand and public rectification notice; repeated default triggers court-ordered judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (declaration de l'impot commercial communal, ICC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the year following the tax year; ACD accommodation extends the final filing end-point to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month capped at 12%; 10% increase of the assessed tax for late filing; risk of tax base estimation ex officio and criminal fine up to EUR 25,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register declaration and annual ownership confirmation (registre des beneficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des beneficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual filing; update within 30 calendar days of any transfer or change; annual confirmation concluded at the anniversary register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and criminal fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 for the SCSp, with parallel fines up to EUR 250,000 for general partners and managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Internal annual accounts, management report and inventory prepared in accordance with Luxembourg accounting law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory organ: the general partner(s); no filing with LBR when the SCSp benefits from the publication exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Partner-claim liability of general partners; loss of evidentiary value of books in court proceedings; tax exposure from unsupported figures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial establishment licence compliance check for the specialty tea salon (autorisation d'etablissement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Middle Classes via the Guichet.lu / Maison de l'etablissement, coordinated with the commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One-off registration at commencement; continuing annual verification of licence conditions and municipal authorisation invoices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or withdrawal of the establishment licence; administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 and potential closure order for unlicensed operation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit by an approved statutory auditor (reviseur d'entreprises agree) is required when the SCSp exceeds any two of three thresholds under the amended Law of 19 December 2002: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net revenue above EUR 8.8 million, average workforce above 50 full-time equivalents; audit also applies when required by the partnership agreement, by a court, or by applicable fund or sector rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP based on the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and the normalized chart of accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is available by election for annual accounts or consolidation purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE law does not impose a recurring calendar filing; however, the SCSp must record every share transfer in its internal register and update the LBR declaration within 30 days of any change. At each anniversary, the general partner shall verify the UBO list against shareholder transfers executed during the year and record a dated confirmation in the minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Management Decisions
Minute Book for partner meetings and written resolutions
Beneficial Owner Register and annual confirmation sheet (RBE)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregated Luxembourg City rate (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); reduced 22.80% on first EUR 175,000 of taxable income where total taxable income does not exceed EUR 200,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Fiscally transparent SCSp: profits flow through to partners, no tax at SCSp level except municipal business tax (ICC) on its Luxembourg PE; small-business reduced CIT band; EUR 175,000 ICC allowance; 17-year loss carryforward; investment tax credit of 8% of eligible investments; no dividend WHT on profit distributions of the transparent SCSp
